source.name: Original texts written for this project
source.attribution: Original text written for this app.
source.notes: Saint names, titles and feast dates come from the liturgical calendar data; biographies were written for this project and should be reviewed by an editor.

saints.name_en: Saints Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen
saints.biography_en: Basil, bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia, and Gregory of Nazianzus became friends as students in Athens and stayed close all their lives. Both defended the faith of the Council of Nicaea about the Holy Trinity. Basil wrote guidance for monks and built a great centre of care for the poor and sick; Gregory, a preacher and poet, served for a time as bishop of Constantinople.
celebrations: Saints Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen, bishops and doctors

saints.biography_en: A priest of Kerala, he helped found the Carmelites of Mary Immaculate, the first religious congregation for men begun in India, and later a congregation of sisters. He opened schools beside parish churches so that every child could learn, set up a printing press and renewed the spiritual life of the Syro-Malabar Church. He was canonized in 2014.
celebrations: IN Saint Kuriakose Elias Chavara, priest

saints.biography_en: A Catalan priest and scholar of law, he joined the Dominicans and gathered the Church's laws into one collection at the request of Pope Gregory IX. He later led the Dominican Order for a short time and spent his long life helping penitents and confessors.

A married convert who became bishop of Poitiers in Gaul, Hilary defended the divinity of Christ against the Arian teaching of his time. Exiled to Asia Minor for his faith, he used the years to write his great work On the Trinity, and returned home to strengthen the Church in the West.
celebrations: Saint Hilary of Poitiers, bishop and doctor

saints.biography_en: Born Neelakanta Pillai near Nagercoil, he served as an official in the court of Travancore. He was baptized in 1745 and took the name Devasahayam, "God is my help". Because he would not give up his faith and treated people of every caste as equals, he was imprisoned and paraded in chains for years before being shot at Aralvaimozhi. In 2022 he became the first Indian lay man to be canonized.

A priest from Goa, he went to Sri Lanka in disguise when Catholics there were persecuted under Dutch rule. For more than twenty years he travelled the island on foot, celebrating the sacraments in secret and caring for the sick during an epidemic. He is honoured as the apostle of Sri Lanka and was canonized in Colombo in 2015.

As a young man Anthony heard the Gospel call to sell everything and follow Christ, and did exactly that. He spent most of his long life in prayer and fasting in the Egyptian desert, and many disciples gathered around him. Through the life written by Saint Athanasius he became the model for monks everywhere.
A layman chosen as bishop of Rome around 236, Fabian organised the care of the poor and the Church's districts in the city. He was among the first to die in the persecution of the Emperor Decius.

A Roman martyr of the early fourth century, Sebastian is remembered by tradition as a soldier who encouraged Christians in prison. Art often shows him pierced with arrows. His tomb on the Appian Way has been honoured since ancient times.

Agnes was a girl of about twelve or thirteen who chose to belong to Christ alone and was put to death in Rome around the year 304. Her courage at so young an age made her one of the best-loved martyrs of the early Church. Her name is said in the Roman Canon of the Mass.

A deacon of the Church of Saragossa in Spain, Vincent was arrested with his bishop during the persecution of Diocletian. He suffered terrible tortures at Valencia without giving up his faith and became one of the most honoured martyrs of Spain.

Bishop of Geneva, Francis taught that holiness is possible for everyone, whatever their state in life. His gentle preaching and his book Introduction to the Devout Life won many hearts. With Saint Jane Frances de Chantal he founded the Order of the Visitation.
celebrations: Saint Francis de Sales, bishop and doctor

saints.biography_en: Timothy and Titus were close companions of Saint Paul on his missionary journeys. Paul left Timothy to lead the Church in Ephesus and Titus to organise the Church in Crete, and wrote to them the letters that bear their names.

Angela gathered young women in Brescia, Italy, to live a consecrated life while staying in their own homes and teaching girls the faith. This Company of Saint Ursula became the Ursulines, one of the first communities of women devoted to education.

An Italian Dominican friar, Thomas taught at Paris and Naples and wrote the Summa Theologiae, which shows how faith and reason work together. He also wrote hymns for the feast of Corpus Christi that are still sung at Benediction. He is one of the great Doctors of the Church.
celebrations: Saint Thomas Aquinas, priest and doctor

saints.biography_en: A priest of Turin, Don Bosco gave his life to poor and abandoned boys, offering them a home, a trade and the faith through kindness rather than punishment. He founded the Salesians and, with Saint Mary Mazzarello, the Daughters of Mary Help of Christians, whose schools are found across India today.

A Benedictine monk from northern France, Ansgar preached the Gospel in Denmark and Sweden and became archbishop of Hamburg-Bremen. His work met with many setbacks, but he never gave up, and he is called the apostle of the North.

Blase was a bishop of Sebaste in Armenia who died as a martyr in the early fourth century. Tradition tells that he healed a boy who was choking on a fish bone, and on his feast the faithful receive a blessing of the throat.

A Portuguese Jesuit, he worked in the Madurai mission and lived as a Tamil teacher of religion, dressing and eating like those he served. Known in Tamil as Arulanandar, he was exiled once and returned, and was beheaded at Oriyur in the Ramanathapuram region in 1693. His shrine at Oriyur draws pilgrims to this day.
celebrations: IN Saint John de Brito, priest and martyr

saints.biography_en: Agatha was a young Christian woman of Catania in Sicily who refused to give up her faith and her vow of virginity. She died under torture in the persecution of Decius in the third century, and her name is said in the Roman Canon.

Born in Vasai near Mumbai, Gonsalo went to Japan as a young man and later became a Franciscan brother. Because he spoke Japanese well, he served as an interpreter for the friars. He was crucified at Nagasaki in 1597 with Saint Paul Miki and companions, and is honoured as the first saint born in India.

Paul Miki was a Japanese Jesuit and preacher. With twenty-five companions, priests, brothers and lay people including boys, he was crucified on a hill at Nagasaki in 1597. From his cross he forgave his persecutors and preached Christ to the crowd.
celebrations: Saints Paul Miki and companions, martyrs

saints.biography_en: A Venetian soldier, Jerome turned to God while a prisoner of war. He then spent his life caring for orphans, the sick and the poor, and founded the Somascan Fathers. He died of an illness caught while nursing the sick.

saints.patronage_en: Sudan and victims of human trafficking
saints.biography_en: Born in Darfur in Sudan, Bakhita was kidnapped as a child and sold several times into slavery. Brought to Italy, she came to know Christ, was baptized and gained her freedom. She became a Canossian sister, known for her gentleness and her readiness to forgive.

Scholastica was the sister of Saint Benedict and, like him, gave her life to God. She led a community of women near Monte Cassino. Saint Gregory the Great tells how, at their last meeting, her prayer brought a storm that kept her brother talking with her through the night about the joys of heaven.

Two brothers from Thessalonica, Cyril and Methodius were sent in the ninth century to preach to the Slavic peoples. They created an alphabet for the Slavonic language and translated the Scriptures and the liturgy into it. They are honoured as co-patrons of Europe.
celebrations: Saints Cyril, monk, and Methodius, bishop

saints.name_en: The Seven Holy Founders of the Servite Order
saints.name_ta: தூய கன்னி மரியாவின் ஊழியர் சபையை நிறுவிய புனிதர் எழுவர்
saints.biography_en: Seven men of Florence left their businesses in the thirteenth century to live a life of prayer and penance on Monte Senario. Devoted to the Mother of God, they founded the Order of Servants of Mary, known as the Servites.
celebrations: Seven Holy Founders of the Servite Order

saints.title_en: bishop and doctor of the Church
saints.biography_en: Peter grew up poor in Ravenna, became a monk and later a cardinal. He worked tirelessly for the reform of the clergy and wrote much on prayer and the monastic life, while always longing to return to his hermitage.
celebrations: Saint Peter Damian, bishop and doctor of the Church

saints.biography_en: Bishop of Smyrna in Asia Minor, Polycarp had known the apostle John. At about eighty-six years old he was arrested and told to curse Christ. He answered that he had served Christ all those years and had never been wronged by him, and he was burned at the stake.

Rani Maria Vattalil, a Franciscan Clarist sister from Kerala, worked among the poor of Madhya Pradesh, helping landless workers to claim their rights. She was stabbed to death on a bus near Indore in 1995. Her family forgave her killer, and she was beatified in 2017.
celebrations: IN Blessed Rani Maria, virgin, martyr

saints.title_en: abbot and doctor of the Church
saints.biography_en: An Armenian monk, priest and poet of the tenth century, Gregory is best known for his Book of Lamentations, a long prayer of sorrow for sin and trust in God's mercy. He was declared a Doctor of the Church in 2015.
celebrations: Saint Gregory of Narek, abbot and doctor of the Church

saints.biography_en: A prince of Poland, Casimir lived simply in the middle of court life, gave generously to the poor and was devoted to the Eucharist and to the Virgin Mary. He died of illness at twenty-five.

Perpetua, a young noblewoman and nursing mother, and Felicity, a pregnant slave, were catechumens arrested in Carthage. Perpetua kept a diary in prison that still survives. They were martyred together in the arena in 203, and both are named in the Roman Canon.

A Portuguese former soldier and bookseller, John was moved to conversion by a sermon in Granada. He opened a house for the sick poor and served them himself. His followers became the Brothers Hospitallers of Saint John of God.

A wife and mother of a noble Roman family, Frances cared for the poor and the sick through war, plague and the loss of her own children. She founded a community of women, the Oblates of Tor de' Specchi, and joined them after her husband's death.

Taken from Britain as a boy and enslaved in Ireland, Patrick found God in his captivity. After escaping he became a priest and returned as a bishop to the people who had enslaved him. He preached throughout Ireland in the fifth century and wrote a moving Confession of his life.

Bishop of Jerusalem in the fourth century, Cyril was exiled several times during the controversies of his age. His instructions to those preparing for baptism and to the newly baptized are among the treasures of the early Church.
celebrations: Saint Cyril of Jerusalem, bishop and doctor

saints.title_en: Husband of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saints.patronage_en: the universal Church, workers and a happy death
saints.biography_en: Joseph, a carpenter of Nazareth and a descendant of David, was the husband of the Virgin Mary and the guardian of Jesus. A just man who listened to God in his dreams, he protected the Holy Family on the flight to Egypt and taught Jesus his trade. The Church honours him as its patron and as the model of workers.
celebrations: Saint Joseph Husband of the Blessed Virgin Mary

saints.biography_en: A Spanish lawyer who was not yet a priest, Turibius was named archbishop of Lima in Peru. He walked thousands of kilometres to visit every part of his diocese, learned local languages, defended the indigenous peoples against abuse and founded the first seminary in the Americas.

From Calabria in southern Italy, Francis lived as a hermit from his youth. Disciples joined him and became the Order of Minims, marked by humility and a lifelong fast. He was known for miracles of healing and was called to France to attend its king at his death.

saints.title_en: bishop and doctor of the Church
saints.biography_en: Isidore was archbishop of Seville in Spain for more than thirty years. He promoted schools and the education of clergy, led Church councils and wrote the Etymologies, an encyclopedia that preserved much ancient learning for the Middle Ages.
celebrations: Saint Isidore, bishop and doctor of the Church

saints.biography_en: A Dominican from Valencia, Vincent travelled through Spain, France, Italy and Switzerland preaching repentance and the coming judgement. Great crowds followed him, and he worked to heal the division in the Church caused by rival claimants to the papacy.

saints.name_en: Saint John Baptist de la Salle
saints.biography_en: A priest of Reims in France, John Baptist gave up his wealth to teach the children of the poor. He founded the Brothers of the Christian Schools and introduced new ways of teaching classes together in the local language. Lasallian schools are now found around the world, including India.
celebrations: Saint John Baptist de la Salle, priest

saints.biography_en: Bishop of Kraków, Stanislaus rebuked King Boleslaus II for his cruelty and injustice. The king killed him while he was celebrating Mass. He is one of the patron saints of Poland.

Pope Martin held a council in Rome in 649 that taught that Christ has a true human will as well as a divine will. The emperor had him arrested and brought to Constantinople, where he was humiliated and then exiled to Crimea, where he died.
celebrations: Saint Martin I, pope and martyr

saints.title_en: bishop and doctor of the Church
saints.biography_en: Born in Aosta in Italy, Anselm became a Benedictine monk and abbot of Bec in Normandy, and then archbishop of Canterbury. He described theology as "faith seeking understanding" and wrote on why God became man. He was twice exiled for defending the freedom of the Church.
celebrations: Saint Anselm of Canterbury, bishop and doctor of the Church

saints.biography_en: Bishop of Prague, Adalbert struggled to bring his people to live the Gospel and twice left his diocese. He went as a missionary to the Prussians on the Baltic coast, where he was killed in 997.

George was a soldier who died as a martyr in Palestine, probably at Lydda, in the early fourth century. The famous story of his fight with a dragon came later as a picture of good overcoming evil. He is honoured by Christians of East and West.

A lawyer known for defending the poor without fee, Fidelis became a Capuchin friar. Sent to preach in Switzerland at a time of religious conflict, he was killed there by those who opposed his mission.
celebrations: Saint Fidelis of Sigmaringen, priest and martyr

saints.biography_en: John Mark accompanied Saint Paul and Saint Barnabas on their first missionary journey and later helped Saint Peter in Rome. He wrote the second Gospel, the shortest and most vivid. Tradition says he founded the Church in Alexandria.

saints.name_ta: மான்போர்ட் நகர் புனித லூயி மரிய கிரிஞ்ஞோ
saints.biography_en: A French priest and tireless preacher of parish missions, Louis taught total consecration to Jesus through Mary in his book True Devotion to Mary. He founded the Montfort Missionaries and, with Blessed Marie-Louise Trichet, the Daughters of Wisdom.
celebrations: Saint Louis Grignon de Montfort, priest

saints.biography_en: A Marist priest from France, Peter went as a missionary to the island of Futuna in the Pacific. He learned the language and cared for the sick, but was clubbed to death when the son of the local king asked for baptism. He is the first martyr of Oceania.
celebrations: Saint Peter Chanel, priest and martyr

saints.title_en: virgin and doctor of the Church
saints.biography_en: Catherine was a Dominican laywoman of Siena, a mystic who cared for the sick and the poor. Though she had little schooling, she wrote letters to popes and rulers and urged Pope Gregory XI to return from Avignon to Rome. Her book, the Dialogue, led to her being named a Doctor of the Church.
celebrations: Saint Catherine of Siena, virgin and doctor of the Church

saints.biography_en: A Dominican friar who became pope in 1566, Pius V put into practice the reforms of the Council of Trent. He published the Roman Catechism, the Breviary and the Missal of 1570, and asked the faithful to pray the Rosary at the time of the battle of Lepanto in 1571.

Bishop of Alexandria for more than forty years, Athanasius defended the faith of the Council of Nicaea that the Son is truly God, equal to the Father. He was sent into exile five times but never gave way. He also wrote the life of Saint Anthony of Egypt.

Philip, from Bethsaida, brought Nathanael to Jesus and at the Last Supper asked to see the Father. James, the son of Alphaeus, is often called James the Less. Both were among the Twelve and gave their lives for the Gospel.

A Spanish priest, John preached across Andalusia and was a guide to many saints, including Teresa of Ávila and John of God. He worked for the formation of priests and was declared a Doctor of the Church in 2012.
celebrations: Saint John of Avila, priest and doctor

saints.biography_en: Nereus and Achilleus were Roman soldiers who became Christians, left the army and were put to death for their faith, probably early in the fourth century. They were buried in the catacomb of Domitilla in Rome.
Pancras was a boy of about fourteen who died as a martyr in Rome early in the fourth century. A church was built over his tomb on the Via Aurelia, and he was widely honoured in the early Church.

After the Ascension, the apostles prayed and cast lots to choose a witness of the Resurrection to take the place of Judas. The lot fell on Matthias, who had followed Jesus from the time of John's baptism (Acts 1).
Pope John I was sent to Constantinople by the Gothic king Theodoric on a difficult mission. On his return the king, displeased, held him at Ravenna, where he died.
celebrations: Saint John I, pope and martyr

saints.biography_en: A Franciscan friar, Bernardine preached throughout Italy to great crowds. He spread devotion to the Holy Name of Jesus, often showing the letters IHS, and called people to give up hatred and make peace.

Christopher Magallanes was a Mexican parish priest who cared for the poor and indigenous people. With twenty-four companions, priests and lay people, he was killed during the persecution of the Church in Mexico in the 1910s and 1920s. He absolved his executioners before he died.
celebrations: Saint Christopher Magallanes and companions, martyrs

saints.biography_en: Rita was married young to a violent man whom she won over by patience. After her husband was murdered and her sons died, she forgave the killers and entered the Augustinian convent at Cascia. She is invoked in difficult and seemingly hopeless situations.

A monk of Jarrow in northern England from childhood, Bede spent his life in prayer, study and teaching. His Ecclesiastical History of the English People is our main source for the early English Church. He is a Doctor of the Church.
celebrations: Saint Bede the Venerable, priest and doctor

saints.biography_en: Hildebrand, a monk who served several popes, was elected pope in 1073. He fought against the buying of Church offices and the control of the Church by princes. Driven from Rome, he died in exile at Salerno, saying he had loved justice and hated iniquity.
A Carmelite nun of Florence, Mary Magdalene received deep mystical experiences of God's love and the Passion of Christ. Through long illness she prayed for the renewal of the Church.
celebrations: Saint Mary Magdalene de Pazzi, virgin

saints.biography_en: Philip came to Rome as a young man and spent sixty years drawing people to God with warmth and humour. He met with friends to pray, read and sing, and from these gatherings came the Congregation of the Oratory. He is called the apostle of Rome.

A monk in Rome, Augustine was sent by Pope Gregory the Great in 597 with companions to bring the Gospel to the English. He baptized King Ethelbert of Kent and became the first archbishop of Canterbury.

Giovanni Battista Montini was elected pope in 1963 and guided the Second Vatican Council to its end. He was the first pope to travel widely, visiting India in 1964, and wrote on evangelisation, human life and the development of peoples. He was canonized in 2018.

Justin was a philosopher from Samaria who found in Christ the truth he had been seeking. He defended the faith in writing and left one of the earliest descriptions of the Sunday Eucharist. He was beheaded in Rome with several of his students.
Marcellinus, a priest, and Peter, an exorcist, were put to death in Rome during the persecution of Diocletian. Their names are said in the Roman Canon.

Charles Lwanga and his companions were young men at the court of the king of Buganda, in today's Uganda. When they refused the king's immoral demands and would not give up their faith, many were burned alive at Namugongo in 1886. Anglican Christians died with them.
celebrations: Saints Charles Lwanga and companions, martyrs

saints.biography_en: An English Benedictine monk, Boniface spent his life preaching the Gospel to the Germanic peoples and organising the Church there as archbishop of Mainz. In old age he went back to Frisia as a missionary and was killed there with his companions.

A worldly cleric from the Rhineland, Norbert changed his life after nearly being killed by lightning. He preached penance, founded the Premonstratensian canons at Prémontré and became archbishop of Magdeburg.

Mariam Thresia of Thrissur in Kerala visited and cared for the sick, the poor and families in trouble, regardless of caste or creed. She founded the Congregation of the Holy Family and bore great suffering in prayer. She was canonized in 2019.
celebrations: IN Blessed Maria Theresa Chiramel, virgin

saints.biography_en: A deacon of Nisibis and Edessa in Syria, Ephrem wrote hymns and poems that taught the faith, many in honour of the Virgin Mary. He is called the Harp of the Holy Spirit and is a Doctor of the Church.

Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, sold his field and gave the money to the apostles, who called him Barnabas, son of encouragement. He welcomed Saul after his conversion and travelled with him on his first missionary journey (Acts 4, 9, 13).

Born in Lisbon, Anthony joined the Franciscans hoping to be a missionary. Instead he became a famous preacher and teacher in Italy and France, and died at Padua aged about thirty-six. He is one of the best-loved saints in Tamil Nadu and is invoked to find what has been lost.
celebrations: Saint Anthony of Padua, priest and doctor

saints.biography_en: A nobleman of Ravenna, Romuald became a monk after his father killed a man in a duel. He founded hermitages and monasteries in Italy, among them Camaldoli, the home of the Camaldolese monks.
Aloysius gave up his place as heir of a noble Italian family to join the Jesuits. As a student in Rome he cared for victims of the plague, caught the disease and died at twenty-three.

saints.name_en: Saints John Fisher and Thomas More
saints.name_ta: புனிதர்கள் ஆயர் ஜான் பிசர், தாமஸ் மூர்
saints.biography_en: John Fisher, bishop of Rochester, and Thomas More, a lawyer and Lord Chancellor of England, refused to accept King Henry VIII as head of the Church in England. Both were beheaded in 1535. More said he died the king's good servant, but God's first.
celebrations: Saints John Fisher, bishop and martyr and Thomas More, martyr

saints.biography_en: A wealthy Roman senator from Bordeaux, Paulinus and his wife Therasia gave their riches to the poor. He settled at Nola in Italy near the tomb of Saint Felix, became its bishop and wrote poems and letters still read today.

Son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, John was the last of the prophets and the forerunner of the Lord. He preached repentance by the Jordan, baptized Jesus and pointed him out as the Lamb of God. He was beheaded by Herod Antipas for speaking the truth. The Church celebrates both his birth and his martyrdom.
celebrations: Birth of Saint John the Baptist
The Beheading of Saint John the Baptist, martyr

saints.biography_en: Patriarch of Alexandria, Cyril led the defence of the truth that Jesus Christ is one person, true God and true man, and that Mary is therefore truly the Mother of God. This was proclaimed at the Council of Ephesus in 431.
celebrations: Saint Cyril of Alexandria, bishop and doctor

saints.title_en: bishop, martyr and doctor of the Church
saints.biography_en: Born in Asia Minor, Irenaeus heard Saint Polycarp preach and later became bishop of Lyons in Gaul. In his work Against Heresies he defended the faith handed down from the apostles. He was declared a Doctor of the Church in 2022 with the title Doctor of Unity.
celebrations: Saint Irenaeus, bishop, martyr and Doctor of the Church

saints.biography_en: Saul of Tarsus, a zealous Pharisee who persecuted the Church, met the risen Christ on the road to Damascus. As Paul he became the apostle to the Gentiles, travelled across the Roman world founding churches and wrote letters that form much of the New Testament. He was martyred in Rome.
celebrations: The Conversion of Saint Paul, apostle

saints.biography_en: Simon, a fisherman of Galilee and brother of Andrew, was called by Jesus and named Peter, the rock on which he would build his Church. He denied the Lord three times and was forgiven, led the apostles after the Resurrection and died as a martyr in Rome, where his tomb lies beneath Saint Peter's Basilica.

saints.name_en: The First Martyrs of the Church of Rome
saints.biography_en: After the great fire of Rome in 64, the Emperor Nero blamed the Christians. Many were put to death in cruel ways. The Church honours these first martyrs of Rome, who died before the apostles Peter and Paul.
celebrations: First Martyrs of the Church of Rome

saints.biography_en: Thomas, called the Twin, at first doubted the Resurrection and then confessed the risen Jesus as "My Lord and my God". By ancient tradition he brought the Gospel to India, founded Christian communities in Kerala and was martyred near Chennai, where his tomb is honoured at San Thome Basilica in Mylapore.

A princess of Aragon and queen of Portugal, Elizabeth bore an unhappy marriage with patience, cared for the poor and more than once made peace between members of her own family at war. As a widow she lived near the Poor Clares at Coimbra.

A doctor who became a priest, Anthony founded the Clerics Regular of Saint Paul, known as the Barnabites, to renew Christian life in Milan. He promoted devotion to the Eucharist and to the letters of Saint Paul.

Maria was an Italian farm girl of eleven who was stabbed when she resisted an attempted assault. Before she died she forgave her attacker. He later repented and was present at her canonization in 1950.
celebrations: Saint Maria Goretti, virgin and martyr

saints.name_en: Saint Augustine Zhao Rong and companions
saints.biography_en: Augustine Zhao Rong was a Chinese soldier who became a priest and died in prison in 1815. He is honoured with 119 other martyrs who died in China between 1648 and 1930: bishops, priests, religious and many lay men, women and children.
celebrations: Saint Augustine Zhao Rong and companions, martyrs

saints.biography_en: Benedict of Nursia left Rome as a young man to seek God in solitude at Subiaco. He later founded the monastery of Monte Cassino and wrote his Rule, built on prayer and work, which shaped monastic life in the West. He is a patron of Europe.

Henry II, Duke of Bavaria and Holy Roman Emperor, ruled with a sense of responsibility before God. He supported the reform of the Church, founded the diocese of Bamberg and was generous to monasteries and the poor.

A soldier with a gambling habit, Camillus was converted and began working in a hospital for incurable patients in Rome. He became a priest and founded the Ministers of the Sick, whose members vow to serve the sick even at the risk of their lives.

A Franciscan from Bagnoregio in Italy, Bonaventure taught theology at Paris, led his order as minister general and became a cardinal. His writings, such as The Journey of the Mind to God, unite learning and love. He is called the Seraphic Doctor.
Apollinaris was the first bishop of Ravenna in Italy. He suffered for the faith and was honoured as a martyr; the basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe was built over his tomb.
A Capuchin friar with a gift for languages, Lawrence preached across Europe, served as a diplomat and led his order. He wrote many sermons and commentaries on Scripture and is a Doctor of the Church.
celebrations: Saint Lawrence of Brindisi, priest and doctor

saints.biography_en: Mary of Magdala followed Jesus after he freed her from seven demons. She stood by the cross and was the first to see the risen Lord, who sent her to tell the apostles. For this she is called the apostle of the apostles, and her memorial was raised to a feast in 2016.

A Swedish noblewoman, wife and mother of eight children, Birgitta (Bridget) received revelations about the Passion of Christ. As a widow she founded the Order of the Most Holy Saviour and went to Rome, where she worked for the renewal of the Church. She is a patron of Europe.
A Maronite monk of Lebanon, Sharbel lived his last twenty-three years as a hermit in prayer, fasting and silence. Many healings have been reported at his tomb in Annaya.

James, son of Zebedee and brother of John, was a fisherman called by Jesus. With Peter and John he witnessed the Transfiguration and the agony in the garden. He was the first of the apostles to die as a martyr, killed by Herod Agrippa (Acts 12). His shrine at Santiago de Compostela draws pilgrims.

saints.title_en: parents of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saints.biography_en: An early Christian tradition gives Joachim and Anne as the names of the parents of the Virgin Mary. The Church honours them as the grandparents of Jesus and as a model of faithful married life.

saints.name_en: Saint Alphonsa of the Immaculate Conception
saints.biography_en: Anna Muttathupadathu of Kerala joined the Franciscan Clarist Congregation and took the name Alphonsa. Nearly all her short religious life was marked by illness, which she accepted with love, uniting her suffering to Christ. In 2008 she became the first woman of Indian origin to be canonized.
celebrations: IN Saint Alphonsa of the Immaculate Conception (Alphonsa Muttathupadathu), virgin

saints.biography_en: Martha, Mary and their brother Lazarus lived at Bethany and welcomed Jesus as a friend. Martha served him, Mary listened at his feet, and Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead. Before that miracle, Martha confessed him as the Christ, the Son of God (John 11).
Bishop of Ravenna in the fifth century, Peter was famous for short, clear sermons; his name means golden word. Many of his sermons on the Creed and the Gospel survive.
celebrations: Saint Peter Chrysologus, bishop and doctor

saints.biography_en: A Basque soldier wounded at Pamplona in 1521, Ignatius read the lives of Christ and the saints while recovering and gave his life to God. He wrote the Spiritual Exercises and, with companions including Francis Xavier, founded the Society of Jesus.

saints.title_en: bishop and doctor of the Church
saints.biography_en: A brilliant Neapolitan lawyer, Alphonsus left the courts to become a priest. He founded the Redemptorists to preach to the rural poor, wrote on moral theology with great mercy for penitents and composed popular works such as The Glories of Mary.
celebrations: Saint Alphonsus Maria de Liguori, bishop and doctor of the Church

saints.biography_en: Bishop of Vercelli in northern Italy, Eusebius lived in community with his clergy. He defended the faith of Nicaea and Saint Athanasius, and was exiled to the East for it.
A French priest, Peter Julian founded the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament and a community of sisters to spread adoration of Christ in the Eucharist and to prepare people for First Communion.

John Vianney struggled with his studies but became parish priest of the small village of Ars in France. Through prayer, penance and long hours in the confessional, he changed the life of his parish, and people came from all over France to see him.
celebrations: Saint Jean Vianney (the Curé of Ars), priest

saints.biography_en: A priest of Vicenza, Cajetan worked for the renewal of the clergy and founded the Theatines, who lived in poverty and trusted entirely in God's providence. He cared for the sick and founded charitable banks to help the poor.
Pope Sixtus II was seized while celebrating the liturgy in a Roman catacomb during the persecution of Valerian and was put to death with four of his deacons in 258.
celebrations: Saint Sixtus II, pope, and companions, martyrs

saints.biography_en: A Castilian priest, Dominic saw the need for preachers who lived poorly and studied deeply. He founded the Order of Preachers, the Dominicans, to proclaim the truth of the Gospel. Tradition links him with the spread of the Rosary.

saints.name_en: Saint Teresa Benedicta of the Cross
saints.biography_en: Edith Stein was a Jewish philosopher who, after reading the life of Saint Teresa of Ávila, became a Catholic and later a Carmelite nun. Arrested by the Nazis, she was killed at Auschwitz in 1942. She is a co-patron of Europe.
celebrations: Saint Teresa Benedicta of the Cross (Edith Stein), virgin and martyr

saints.biography_en: Lawrence was one of the seven deacons of Rome, in charge of caring for the poor. Told to hand over the Church's treasures, he is said to have presented the poor. He was martyred a few days after Pope Sixtus II in 258.

Clare of Assisi left her noble family to follow Saint Francis in poverty. She founded the Poor Ladies, now called the Poor Clares, and led them for forty years at San Damiano, trusting in Christ present in the Eucharist.

A French noblewoman widowed with four children, Jane found a guide in Saint Francis de Sales. Together they founded the Order of the Visitation, open to women who could not bear the severe life of other convents.
celebrations: Saint Jane Frances de Chantal, religious

saints.biography_en: Pope Pontian and the Roman priest Hippolytus had been on opposing sides of a bitter dispute in the Roman Church. Both were sent to the mines of Sardinia during a persecution in 235, where they died reconciled, and both are honoured as martyrs.
celebrations: Saints Pontian, pope, and Hippolytus, priest, martyrs

saints.biography_en: A Polish Franciscan, Maximilian founded the Militia of the Immaculata and a great friary and publishing centre at Niepokalanów, and was a missionary in Japan. Imprisoned at Auschwitz, he offered his life in place of a man with a family who had been condemned to die, and died in the starvation bunker.
celebrations: Saint Maximilian Mary Kolbe, priest and martyr

saints.biography_en: Stephen was the first king of Hungary. He was baptized as a young man, worked to bring his people to the faith, founded dioceses and monasteries and was known for his care of the poor.

A French priest and missionary preacher, John Eudes founded a congregation of priests to form seminarians and an order of sisters to help women in need. He promoted devotion to the Hearts of Jesus and Mary and wrote liturgical texts in their honour.

saints.title_en: abbot and doctor of the Church
saints.biography_en: Bernard entered the Cistercian monastery of Cîteaux with some thirty companions and was soon sent to found Clairvaux. His preaching and writings on the love of God and on the Virgin Mary earned him the name Mellifluous Doctor, honey-sweet teacher.
celebrations: Saint Bernard of Clairvaux, abbot and doctor of the Church

saints.biography_en: Giuseppe Sarto, the son of a poor family, served as a parish priest and bishop before being elected pope in 1903. His motto was to restore all things in Christ. He encouraged frequent Communion and allowed children to receive it from the age of reason.

Rose was a young woman of Lima who lived a life of prayer and penance as a Dominican laywoman and cared for the sick and poor in her family home. She was the first person born in the Americas to be canonized.

Bartholomew was one of the Twelve and is often identified with Nathanael, of whom Jesus said, "Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit" (John 1). Ancient traditions say he preached in India and Armenia, where he died as a martyr.

A Spanish priest working in Rome, Joseph opened a free school for poor children in 1597, one of the first in Europe. He founded the Piarists to continue this work, and remained faithful through great trials within his own order.

Louis IX became king of France as a boy. He ruled with justice, cared personally for the poor and sick and built the Sainte-Chapelle to house relics of the Passion. He died of illness at Tunis on crusade.
Monica, a Christian woman of North Africa, prayed for many years with tears for the conversion of her son Augustine. She followed him to Italy and saw him baptized in Milan before she died at Ostia.

saints.title_en: bishop and doctor of the Church
saints.biography_en: Born in Thagaste in North Africa, Augustine sought truth through many years of restless searching. Moved by the prayers of his mother Monica and the preaching of Saint Ambrose, he was baptized in 387. As bishop of Hippo he wrote the Confessions and The City of God, which shaped Christian thought for centuries.
celebrations: Saint Augustine of Hippo, bishop and doctor of the Church

saints.biography_en: Rose Eluvathingal of Thrissur in Kerala joined the Congregation of the Mother of Carmel and took the name Euphrasia. Known as the praying mother, she spent long hours before the Blessed Sacrament and gave wise counsel to all who came to her. She was canonized in 2014.

A Roman prefect who became a monk, Gregory was elected pope in 590 during plague and war. He cared for the hungry, sent Augustine to bring the faith to the English and wrote much on pastoral care. He called himself the servant of the servants of God.
celebrations: Saint Gregory the Great, pope and doctor

saints.biography_en: Born in Skopje, Teresa came to India as a Loreto sister and taught in Kolkata. In 1946 she heard a call to serve the poorest of the poor, and in 1950 she founded the Missionaries of Charity, who care for the dying, the sick and abandoned children around the world. She was canonized in 2016.
celebrations: IN Saint Teresa of Calcutta, virgin

saints.biography_en: A Spanish Jesuit, Peter served for forty years in Cartagena, Colombia, where ships brought enslaved Africans. He met the ships, cared for the sick, taught the faith and called himself the slave of the slaves forever.

A priest of Antioch, John was so powerful a preacher that he was called Chrysostom, golden mouth. As archbishop of Constantinople he spoke out against the abuse of wealth and power, and died in exile. He is a Doctor of the Church.
celebrations: Saint John Chrysostom, bishop and doctor

saints.biography_en: Pope Cornelius and Cyprian, bishop of Carthage, both held that Christians who had denied the faith under persecution could be forgiven after penance. Cornelius died in exile in 253; Cyprian was beheaded in 258. Both are named in the Roman Canon.
celebrations: Saints Cornelius, pope, and Cyprian, bishop, martyrs

saints.title_en: virgin and doctor of the Church
saints.biography_en: A German Benedictine abbess, Hildegard recorded her visions, composed music and wrote on medicine and the natural world. She counselled popes and emperors and was declared a Doctor of the Church in 2012.
celebrations: Saint Hildegard of Bingen, Virgin and Doctor

saints.biography_en: An Italian Jesuit and cardinal, Robert taught and defended the Catholic faith during the Reformation. He wrote catechisms that were used for centuries and lived simply, giving much to the poor. He is a Doctor of the Church.
celebrations: Saint Robert Bellarmine, bishop and doctor

saints.biography_en: Januarius was a bishop of Benevento in southern Italy who died as a martyr around the year 305. He is the patron of Naples, where a relic of his blood is venerated.

saints.name_en: Saints Andrew Kim Taegon, Paul Chong Hasang and companions
saints.name_ta: புனிதர்கள் மறைப்பணியாளர் ஆன்ரு கிம் தே கோன், பவுல் சோங் காசாங், தோழர்கள்
saints.biography_en: The Catholic faith reached Korea through lay people who studied Christian books. In the persecutions of the nineteenth century thousands died. Andrew Kim Taegon, the first Korean priest, and Paul Chong Hasang, a lay leader, are honoured with 101 companions canonized in 1984.
celebrations: Saint Andrew Kim Taegon, priest, and Paul Chong Hasang and companions, martyrs

saints.biography_en: Matthew, also called Levi, was a tax collector when Jesus called him to follow. He left everything, gave a banquet for Jesus and his friends, and became one of the Twelve. The first Gospel bears his name.
celebrations: Saint Matthew the Evangelist, Apostle, Evangelist

saints.biography_en: A Capuchin friar of southern Italy, Padre Pio bore the wounds of Christ for fifty years. He spent long hours hearing confessions, led many to God and founded a hospital, the House for the Relief of Suffering, at San Giovanni Rotondo.
celebrations: Saint Pio of Pietrelcina (Padre Pio), priest

saints.biography_en: Cosmas and Damian were brothers, by tradition twins, who practised medicine without charging fees. They died as martyrs in Syria, probably around the year 300, and are named in the Roman Canon.

A French priest, Vincent devoted his life to the poor. He founded the Congregation of the Mission to preach to country people and, with Saint Louise de Marillac, the Daughters of Charity to serve the sick and poor. He is the patron of all charitable societies.
Lorenzo Ruiz, a married layman from Manila, went to Japan with Dominican missionaries. With fifteen companions he was put to death at Nagasaki in the 1630s. He is the first Filipino saint.
celebrations: Saints Lawrence Ruiz and companions, martyrs

saints.biography_en: Wenceslaus, duke of Bohemia in the tenth century, ruled as a Christian prince and helped the poor. He was killed by his brother on the way to Mass and is the patron of the Czech people.

Michael, whose name asks "Who is like God?", defends God's people against evil (Daniel 12, Revelation 12). Gabriel announced the births of John the Baptist and of Jesus (Luke 1). Raphael guided Tobias and healed Tobit (Tobit 12). The Church honours the three together.
celebrations: Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, Archangels

saints.biography_en: Jerome was a scholar of great learning and strong temper. At the request of Pope Damasus he revised the Latin Bible and later translated much of it from Hebrew; this version became known as the Vulgate. He lived his last years in Bethlehem and wrote that ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ.

saints.name_en: Saint Thérèse of the Child Jesus
saints.biography_en: Thérèse entered the Carmelite convent of Lisieux at fifteen and died of tuberculosis at twenty-four. Her little way of doing small things with great love, told in her Story of a Soul, has helped countless people. She is patron of the missions and a Doctor of the Church.
celebrations: Saint Thérèse of the Child Jesus, virgin and doctor

saints.biography_en: The son of a rich merchant of Assisi, Francis gave up everything to live in poverty and joy, serving lepers and preaching peace. He founded the Friars Minor and, with Saint Clare, the Poor Clares. He sang of God in all creation and received the wounds of Christ two years before he died.

A Polish sister of the Congregation of Our Lady of Mercy, Faustina recorded in her diary her experiences of Jesus and his message of Divine Mercy. From her came the image of the Merciful Jesus with the words "Jesus, I trust in you".

A teacher at the cathedral school of Reims, Bruno left with a few companions to live in solitude in the mountains near Grenoble. There he founded the Carthusians, who unite the life of hermits with life in community.

Denis was sent from Rome to Gaul in the third century and became the first bishop of Paris. He was beheaded with the priest Rusticus and the deacon Eleutherius, and the abbey of Saint-Denis was built over their tomb.

saints.title_en: priest and doctor of the Church
saints.biography_en: An Anglican priest and leader of the Oxford Movement, John Henry Newman was received into the Catholic Church in 1845. He founded the Oratory in England, wrote on faith, conscience and the development of doctrine, and was made a cardinal. He was canonized in 2019 and declared a Doctor of the Church in 2025.
celebrations: Saint John Henry Newman, Priest and Doctor of the Church

saints.biography_en: A pharmacist's assistant who became a priest in Lucca, John founded the Clerks Regular of the Mother of God and taught the faith to children and adults. He also helped prepare the way for the Church's college for the missions in Rome.

Angelo Roncalli, the son of farmers, served as a papal diplomat and patriarch of Venice before being elected pope in 1958. Known for his warmth and humour, he called the Second Vatican Council and wrote on peace among all peoples. He was canonized in 2014.

Callistus, a former slave, was put in charge of a Christian cemetery on the Appian Way, now called the catacomb of Saint Callistus. As pope he taught that God's mercy is open to every repentant sinner. He died as a martyr.
celebrations: Saint Callistus I, pope and martyr

saints.biography_en: Teresa of Ávila entered the Carmelite convent as a young woman and, after years of struggle in prayer, began a reform of her order with houses of poverty and prayer. Her writings, such as The Way of Perfection and The Interior Castle, made her the first woman named a Doctor of the Church.
celebrations: Saint Teresa of Jesus, virgin and doctor

saints.biography_en: Known as Kunjachan, he was a priest of the diocese of Palai in Kerala who spent his life among the Dalit people of Ramapuram, visiting their homes, teaching and caring for them. He was beatified in 2006.
A duchess of Silesia, Hedwig used her wealth to found monasteries and hospitals and lived simply in the midst of court life. After her husband's death she lived at the Cistercian convent of Trebnitz.

A Visitation nun at Paray-le-Monial in France, Margaret Mary received revelations of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, who showed her his love for all people. From her came the devotion of the First Fridays and the feast of the Sacred Heart.

Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, was taken to Rome to be thrown to wild beasts early in the second century. On the journey he wrote seven letters to the churches about unity, the bishop and the Eucharist, calling himself God's wheat.
celebrations: Saint Ignatius of Antioch, bishop and martyr

saints.biography_en: Luke, a physician, was a companion of Saint Paul. He wrote the third Gospel, which tells of Christ's mercy to the poor and outcast and gives us the Annunciation and the Magnificat, and the Acts of the Apostles.

saints.name_en: Saints Jean de Brébeuf, Isaac Jogues and companions
saints.name_ta: புனிதர்கள் மறைப்பணியாளர்கள் பிரபூபு ஜான், ஈசாக்கு ஜோகு, தோழர்கள்
saints.biography_en: Jean de Brébeuf, Isaac Jogues and six companions, French Jesuit priests and lay helpers, worked among the Huron and Iroquois peoples of North America. They were killed between 1642 and 1649.
celebrations: Saints Jean de Brébeuf, Isaac Jogues, priests and martyrs; and their companions, martyrs

saints.biography_en: An Italian priest and preacher, Paul founded the Passionists, whose members vow to keep alive the memory of the Passion of Christ. He also founded a community of contemplative Passionist nuns.
celebrations: Saint Paul of the Cross, priest

saints.biography_en: Karol Wojtyła of Poland, a priest, philosopher and bishop of Kraków, was elected pope in 1978. He travelled to every continent, visiting India in 1986 and 1999, and wrote extensively on human dignity and the family. He established Divine Mercy Sunday and was canonized in 2014.
A lawyer and governor of Perugia, John became a Franciscan after imprisonment. He preached throughout Europe and, in old age, helped lead the defence of Belgrade in 1456, dying of plague soon after.

A Spanish weaver who became a priest, Anthony preached missions across Catalonia and the Canary Islands and founded the Claretian Missionaries. As archbishop of Santiago de Cuba he worked for the poor and against slavery.

Simon, called the Zealot, and Jude, also called Thaddeus, were among the Twelve. The Letter of Jude is traditionally linked with Jude. By tradition both preached in Persia and died as martyrs; Jude is invoked in desperate situations.
celebrations: Saint Simon and Saint Jude, apostles

saints.biography_en: Born in Lima to a Spanish father and a mother of African descent, Martin faced prejudice from childhood. As a Dominican brother he cared for the sick, the poor, orphans and even animals with tireless love.

Charles was made a cardinal young by his uncle, Pope Pius IV, and helped bring the Council of Trent to its end. As archbishop of Milan he founded seminaries and reformed clergy and people, and stayed to serve the sick during the plague.

Pope from 440 to 461, Leo taught clearly that Christ is one person in two natures, divine and human, which the Council of Chalcedon accepted. He met Attila the Hun near Mantua and persuaded him to turn back from Rome.
celebrations: Saint Leo the Great, pope and doctor

saints.biography_en: As a young soldier Martin cut his cloak in two to share it with a freezing beggar, and that night saw Christ wearing it. He left the army, became a monk and, as bishop of Tours, founded monasteries and preached throughout Gaul.

A Ukrainian monk of the Byzantine rite, Josaphat became archbishop of Polotsk and worked for unity between Eastern Christians and the Church of Rome. He was killed by opponents of that unity at Vitebsk.
A German Dominican, Albert studied and taught philosophy, theology and the natural sciences, and was the teacher of Thomas Aquinas. He served as bishop of Regensburg and is a Doctor of the Church.
celebrations: Saint Albert the Great, bishop and doctor

saints.biography_en: Gertrude was entrusted as a child to the convent of Helfta in Germany, where she became a nun and a scholar. Her writings on the love of the Heart of Jesus helped prepare devotion to the Sacred Heart.
An English princess who became queen of Scotland, Margaret was a devoted wife and mother of eight. She cared daily for orphans and the poor and worked for the renewal of the Church in Scotland.

saints.patronage_en: Franciscan Third Order and charitable works
saints.biography_en: A Hungarian princess married to a German prince, Elizabeth gave generously to the poor. Widowed at twenty, she built a hospital at Marburg and served the sick herself as a Franciscan tertiary until her death at twenty-four.

Cecilia was a Roman virgin and martyr of the early Church whose memory has been honoured since ancient times. Tradition tells that she sang to God in her heart, and so she became the patron of music. She is named in the Roman Canon.

Clement was one of the first bishops of Rome after Saint Peter. His letter to the Church of Corinth, written around the year 96, calls the Christians there to peace and order and is one of the oldest Christian writings outside the New Testament.
celebrations: Saint Clement I, pope and martyr

saints.biography_en: An Irish monk, Columban left his homeland as a missionary pilgrim and founded monasteries in Gaul, including Luxeuil, and finally at Bobbio in Italy. His strict rule and missionary zeal shaped the Church in Europe.

saints.name_ta: புனிதர்கள் மறைப்பணியாளர் ஆன்ரு டுங் லாக், தோழர்கள்
saints.biography_en: Andrew Dung-Lac, a Vietnamese priest, is honoured with 116 companions who died for the faith in Vietnam between 1745 and 1862. They included bishops, priests, catechists, and married men and women.
celebrations: Saint Andrew Dung-Lac and his companions, martyrs

saints.biography_en: Tradition tells of Catherine, a learned young woman of Alexandria who answered the philosophers of the emperor and brought many to faith. She died as a martyr in the early fourth century.

A fisherman of Bethsaida and a disciple of John the Baptist, Andrew was among the first called by Jesus and brought his brother Simon Peter to him (John 1). Tradition says he preached in Greece and was crucified at Patras.

A Basque nobleman and companion of Saint Ignatius, Francis was one of the first Jesuits. Arriving in Goa in 1542, he preached along the coast of Tamil Nadu among the fishing people, then in Malaysia, the Moluccas and Japan. He died off the coast of China, and his body lies in the Basilica of Bom Jesus in Goa. He is a patron of India.

John of Damascus, born into a Christian family serving the caliph, became a monk near Jerusalem. He defended the veneration of holy images and wrote The Fount of Knowledge, a summary of the faith of the Eastern Fathers. He is a Doctor of the Church.
celebrations: Saint John Damascene, priest and doctor

saints.biography_en: Nicholas was bishop of Myra in Asia Minor in the fourth century. Many stories tell of his secret generosity, such as giving dowries to three poor girls. He is honoured in East and West and is the origin of the figure of Santa Claus.

Ambrose was the Roman governor of Milan when the people chose him as bishop, though he was not yet baptized. He became a great pastor, preacher and writer of hymns, defended the Church against emperors and baptized Saint Augustine. He is a Doctor of the Church.

Juan Diego Cuauhtlatoatzin was an indigenous man of Mexico. In 1531 the Virgin Mary appeared to him at Tepeyac, and her image appeared on his cloak, venerated today as Our Lady of Guadalupe. He spent the rest of his life caring for her shrine.
Pope from 366 to 384, Damasus honoured the tombs of the martyrs with inscriptions he wrote himself and asked Saint Jerome to revise the Latin translation of the Bible.

Lucy, a young Christian of Syracuse in Sicily, gave her goods to the poor and died as a martyr in the persecution of Diocletian. Her name means light, and she is invoked for the eyes. She is named in the Roman Canon.
celebrations: Saint Lucy of Syracuse, virgin and martyr

saints.biography_en: A Spanish Carmelite friar, John worked with Saint Teresa of Ávila to renew their order and was imprisoned by his own brothers for it. His poems and writings, such as The Dark Night and The Spiritual Canticle, describe the soul's journey to union with God. He is a Doctor of the Church.
celebrations: Saint John of the Cross, priest and doctor

saints.biography_en: A Dutch Jesuit, Peter worked for the renewal of the Catholic faith in Germany and central Europe. He founded colleges and wrote catechisms that were used for centuries. He is a Doctor of the Church.
celebrations: Saint Peter Canisius, priest and doctor

saints.biography_en: A priest and professor at the University of Kraków, John was known for his learning, humility and generosity to the poor, often giving away his own food and clothing.

Stephen, full of grace and the Holy Spirit, was one of the seven chosen to serve the poor in Jerusalem. Accused before the council, he saw the heavens opened and was stoned to death, praying for his killers as Saul looked on (Acts 6–7). He is the first martyr.

John, son of Zebedee and brother of James, was the disciple whom Jesus loved. He stood at the cross, where Jesus gave Mary into his care, and ran to the empty tomb. The fourth Gospel, three letters and the Book of Revelation are linked with his name.
celebrations: Saint John the Apostle and evangelist

saints.biography_en: When Herod heard of the birth of the King of the Jews, he ordered the killing of the boys of Bethlehem under two years old (Matthew 2). The Church honours these children as martyrs who died in place of Christ.
Thomas was chancellor of England and a friend of King Henry II. Made archbishop of Canterbury, he defended the freedom of the Church against the king and was murdered in his cathedral in 1170.
celebrations: Saint Thomas Becket, bishop and martyr

saints.biography_en: Sylvester was pope from 314 to 335, when the Church first gained freedom under the Emperor Constantine. In his time the great basilicas of Rome, including the Lateran, were built.
